$comment: EVERY PROPOSAL BRANCH IS NAMED do-not-merge/<x>, and the name is the first thing anyone sees — in a branch list, in a PR title, in a checkout. The gate reads this table for permission; the prefix reads to a person.
Branches that are ALLOWED to cross lane boundaries, and the only place that
permission exists. scripts/check-lanes.mjs reads this file, matches the branch
it is running on, and reports every cross-lane file it finds as a PROPOSAL
instead of failing on it.
THE PERMISSION IS NARROW ON PURPOSE:
- a branch not listed here fails on the first cross-lane file, as always
- a listed branch still fails on a lane it did not declare
- main can never be listed; the gate refuses the whole file if it is
- every proposed file is PRINTED on every run, so nothing is ever silent
WHAT A PROPOSAL BRANCH IS FOR. The lane law makes merge conflicts
structurally impossible by giving each developer one folder. That works while
everyone is building. It has no answer for 'here is what your folder could
look like' - which is a normal, useful thing for one developer to offer
another, and the only honest way to offer it is as code somebody can read,
run and decide about. These branches carry that offer. They are never merged;
each owner takes what they want.
AUTHORSHIP IS NEVER FORGED. Every commit on a proposal branch is authored by
whoever actually wrote it. The gate still attributes it correctly and still
names the lane it reached into.

branches.why: The integration line for a cross-lane proposal. Every product folder is worked on here so the four can be made to agree with each other and with app/shared/ at once. Never merged to main: each owner receives their own folder as something to copy or refuse.
Product A's half of the v0.0.2 proposal - the booking app, worked on so its owner can read a working folder rather than a list of defects.
Product B's half of the v0.0.2 proposal - the staff scheduling dashboard.
Product C's half of the v0.0.2 proposal - the member support assistant.
